- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) or zero, model often underestimates or ignores downside risk; increase downward bias or add volatility buffer.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overcorrects with steep upward trend; cap forecast growth or introduce lagged mean reversion.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 80), model often fails to adjust; apply downward bias or use moving average smoothing.
- If forecast is rising steadily but true outcome shows early divergence (e.g., first 3–5 days), model often overshoots; reduce initial forecast slope or add early correction factor.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, model tends to assume linear continuation; if sentiment is volatile or mixed, introduce stochastic or stepwise adjustment based on sentiment clusters.
